elements.element: Audit frequency may not exceed once in any twelve (12) month period.
elements.evidence: The clause permits inspection “not more than once in any twelve (12) month period.”

elements.element: Customer must receive at least thirty (30) days' prior notice.
elements.evidence: The clause requires “no less than thirty (30) days prior” notice.

elements.element: The audit notice must be written.
The audit must occur during Customer's business hours.
elements.evidence: Inspection is limited to “the Company's normal business hours.”

elements.element: The audit must be conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: HDI may exercise the right only “through an independent third-party auditor.”

elements.element: The auditor must be bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: The auditor must be “bound by written confidentiality obligations.”

elements.element: Vendor must bear the audit costs where underpayment does not exceed 5%.
elements.evidence: The clause requires all inspection fees incurred by HDI to be borne by HDI, including where underpayment does not exceed 5%.

elements.element: Audit costs may be shifted to Customer only where underpayment exceeds 5%.
elements.evidence: The clause does not permit any cost-shifting to Customer, which is more protective of Customer than permitting it above the 5% threshold.

elements.element: The audit must not include direct access to Customer's systems.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly provides that an inspection “shall not include direct access to the Company's systems.”

elements.element: Audit frequency may not exceed once per year.
elements.evidence: The once-in-any-twelve-month limit is at least as restrictive as once per year.

elements.element: Customer must receive at least fifteen (15) days' prior notice.
elements.evidence: The clause requires at least thirty days' prior written notice, exceeding the fallback notice period.

elements.element: Vendor must bear the audit costs where underpayment does not exceed 10%.
elements.evidence: The clause requires all inspection fees incurred by HDI to be borne by HDI, including where underpayment does not exceed 10%.

elements.element: Audit costs may be shifted to Customer only where underpayment exceeds 10%.
elements.evidence: The clause permits no cost-shifting to Customer, which is more protective than the fallback's conditional cost-shifting allowance.

result.reason: The operative language satisfies every preferred and fallback requirement. Requiring HDI to bear all inspection fees is more protective of Customer than either threshold-based cost-shifting position. The redline is not minimal because it additionally requires off-site inspection “wherever possible,” which is not needed once direct systems access is expressly prohibited. Drafting quality is reduced by the redundant construction “may ... have the right,” the vague “wherever possible” qualifier, and the potentially narrow reference to records “of the Company's General Manager,” although that wording was inherited from the original clause.
